subject.title: fix(agents): cron and agent runs mark successful exec commands with semantic nonzero exits as failed

question: Should the shared tool-result contract treat an explicit `status: "completed"` as authoritative over a nonzero `exitCode` for all current tool-result producers, with fatal conditions required to emit a failure status or explicit failure field?
rationale: The patch is mechanically narrow and the supplied exec/cron proof is positive, but the changed helper is shared across agent runtimes and controls user-visible warnings plus persisted cron outcomes. Choosing its cross-producer terminal-state contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt completed as authoritative
options.body: Merge this PR and require producers with genuine failures to emit a failure status, timeout, error field, or explicit unsuccessful flag.

options.title: Limit the exception to exec
options.body: Keep nonzero exits fatal in the generic classifier and add an exec-specific signal or classification path if only shell semantics should change.

options.title: Define a richer terminal contract first
options.body: Pause this PR while maintainers specify a dedicated semantic-exit outcome that preserves generic failure detection without relying on an overloaded completed status.

recommendation.title: Adopt completed as authoritative
recommendation.body: Merge this PR and require producers with genuine failures to emit a failure status, timeout, error field, or explicit unsuccessful flag.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged structured-terminal-state refactor associated with this shared classifier is the strongest available ownership signal.
